dedupe_keys.name: citywide particulate matter on underground subway platforms in shanghai

description: This study by Tianchen Qin, Ran Tu, An Wang and colleagues, with authors from institutions in China, Hong Kong, Canada and the US, published in npj Sustainable Mobility and Transport, investigates indoor air quality in the Shanghai subway through year-round monitoring of PM2.5 and PM10 at representative underground stations. Coverage: concentrations were markedly higher indoors, peaking during winter weekday morning rush hours, with indoor to outdoor ratios above one; an interpretable machine learning model identifies platform screen door design and train frequency as the dominant factors; combined with network-wide operational data and passenger boarding records it gives city-scale PM levels and commuter exposure, and point-of-interest data show the highest exposure near residential zones and more pollution where commercial density is high. Format and access: an open article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: the abstract was the part read and the monitoring data are not described as released. The station factors and exposure estimates can guide ventilation and operations in subway hazard exposure models. It relates to the NYU northeastern US subway PM2.5 data in the catalogue.
